title: Colombia dengue cases near 100,000: Interventions, including vaccination intensified - Outbreak News Today
text:
Colombia dengue cases near 100,000: Interventions, including vaccination intensified 
 Subscribe Sign in Latin America and the Caribbean Colombia dengue cases near 100,000: Interventions, including vaccination intensified
 Robert Herriman Nov 15, 2026 Share Colombia’s Ministry of Health and Social Protection has intensified vaccination efforts, the control of mosquito breeding sites, and the early detection of dengue cases in response to the increased risk associated with the El Niño phenomenon.
 The Ministry reported that 98,096 infections and 73 confirmed deaths have been recorded in the country, with cases concentrated in the Caribbean region, as well as in the departments of Meta and Tolima.
 The plan includes the continued vaccination of 9- and 10-year-old children across 23 prioritized territories. The strategy, which began in a phased manner in 2026, aims to expand coverage to 76 municipalities by April 2027 as part of the response in areas with high transmission rates.

 The Institute of Hydrology, Meteorology and Environmental Studies (IDEAM) officially declared the onset of the El Niño phenomenon on October 8. Reduced rainfall and potential water supply issues may lead households to store water in containers; if these are left uncovered or are not cleaned regularly, they become breeding grounds for the Aedes aegypti mosquito. 
 The presence of all four serotypes of the virus in Colombia places additional pressure on health authorities. According to data released by the Ministry of Health, 13% of all reported cases and 23% of all reported deaths occurred during the month of October.
 “We must take action before a dengue case becomes complicated,” stated Gloria Nayibe Prado Pino, Deputy Minister of Public Health and Primary Care. She urged families to eliminate breeding sites, protect stored water, and seek medical attention at the first sign of warning symptoms.
 Of the cases included in the INS report, 59,472 showed no warning signs, 37,443 presented with warning signs, and 979 developed severe dengue. The department of Meta topped the national list with 14,131 infections, followed by Bolívar with 9,704; Santander with 7,488; Cesar with 6,745; and Norte de Santander with 6,094.
 In 25 territorial entities, the number of cases increased by more than 30%. These territories include Atlántico, Magdalena, Tolima, Valle del Cauca, and Sucre.
 The situation in the Caribbean region is a particular cause for concern. Atlántico recorded 4,009 cases and seven confirmed deaths, while Barranquilla reported 3,080 infections and one death. Together, these two areas accounted for 7,089 cases and eight deaths, with an additional three deaths currently under investigation.
 The Ministry is coordinating with the INS, territorial authorities, health insurance providers (EPS), and healthcare service providers (IPS) to implement measures for the early identification of patients, aiming to prevent the infection from progressing to a severe stage.

 The response includes interventions in homes, schools, and hospitals to remove or treat containers where water might otherwise accumulate. Priority will also be given to monitoring children and adolescents, pregnant women, individuals over the age of 60, and patients with other underlying health conditions—groups that require special observation due to the potential for clinical deterioration.
 Vaccination serves as a complementary measure. Authorities emphasized that it does not replace preventive efforts at home or the need to seek timely medical attention if symptoms consistent with the disease appear.
 The Ministry of Health will continue to track the progression of dengue and will adjust interventions in areas where the risk increases. The primary goal of the strategy is to prevent deaths through timely prevention, diagnosis, and care.
